about.title: Madera Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Falls happen fast, but the aftermath can drag on for months — torn ligaments, fractured wrists, or a hip injury that changes how you move through daily life. In Madera, these cases often arise at grocery stores, apartment complexes near Cleveland Avenue, or businesses along Rt 145 where foot traffic is heavy. California law requires the injured person to show the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn visitors in time. That's why what you do right after a fall matters: photos of the spill, wet floor, broken step, or uneven pavement; names of witnesses; and a written incident report if the property has staff on site. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect you, at no cost, with an independent Madera-area attorney who can evaluate your fall, help you understand your options, and pursue a claim on a contingency basis if you decide to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About a Madera Fall

items.title: Notice Is the Whole Case
items.desc: California requires proof the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney can dig into maintenance logs, prior complaints, and inspection records to establish that notice.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many stores and complexes overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly gives an attorney the chance to send a preservation letter before that evidence is gone.

items.title: Comparative Fault Cuts Both Ways
items.desc: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still recover even if you're found partly at fault, though it reduces the amount. An attorney works to keep the fault conversation fair and evidence-based.

items.question: How long do I have to file a premises liability claim in Madera?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If a government-owned property was involved, such as a public sidewalk or county building, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim notice. It's worth speaking with an attorney soon so nothing gets missed.

items.question: What if I fell but didn't take pictures right away?
items.answer: It's not ideal, but it's not necessarily fatal to a claim. An attorney can still request incident reports, maintenance records, and any available surveillance footage from the property. Witness statements and medical records documenting the timing of your injury also help fill in the picture.

items.question: Does it matter that my fall happened near a busy Madera corridor like Cleveland Avenue?
items.answer: High foot traffic near corridors like Cleveland Avenue or Rt 145 doesn't change the legal standard, but it can affect how quickly hazards should have been noticed and cleaned up. Busier locations often have more frequent inspection duties, which an attorney can factor into building your case.
